scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that trash limits help, then argues they are not the best solution alone; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Mountains of household waste are among the most visible problems our towns now face.
Some people claim that the best way to solve waste problems is for towns to impose strict limits on the trash they accept from each household.
I agree that limiting waste can help, but I do not believe strict limits alone are the best solution.
First, limiting household trash can genuinely reduce the waste a town produces.
When people must keep within a fixed limit, they think harder about what they throw away.
For example, a household charged for extra bags will quickly learn to waste less and recycle more.
This shows that clear limits can push people to change their wasteful habits.
Less trash also means lower costs and less harm to the land and air around a town.
Strict limits send a clear signal that waste is everyone's responsibility.
To this extent, trash limits are a useful tool.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why limits alone are not enough

sentences.text: Second, however, strict limits alone are far from the best way to solve the problem.
Limits punish waste but do little to give people better alternatives.
Consider a family that wants to waste less but has no recycling service to make it possible.
Such cases show that limits without support can simply lead to illegal dumping instead.
Recycling programmes, better packaging, and public education often reduce waste more effectively.
Strict rules can also fall hardest on large or poor families with little control over their waste.
The best solution, then, combines limits with real alternatives and education.
In conclusion, strict limits on household trash can usefully reduce waste.
But limits alone are not the best answer, since people also need better alternatives.
The wisest approach joins sensible limits with recycling, education, and less wasteful products.
